# Long service leave

Learn more about long service leave and where to go for help.

## About long service leave

An employee gets [long service leaveA period of paid leave that is available to employees who have worked for the same business for a period of time. The length of time would depend on the employee’s award or registered agreement.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/392 "long service leave") after a long period of working for the same employer.

Most employees’ entitlement to long service leave comes from long service leave laws in each state or territory. These laws set out:

- how long an employee must work to get long service leave (for example, after 7 years)
- how much long service leave the employee gets.

In some states and territories, [long serving casualsAn employee whose been employed by the same employer on a regular and systematic basis for at least 12 months.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/393 "long term casuals") are eligible for long service leave.

To find out about long service leave entitlements, contact the long service leave agency in your state or territory:

- Australian Capital Territory: [WorkSafe ACT](https://www.worksafe.act.gov.au/laws-and-compliance/long-service-leave)
- New South Wales: [NSW Industrial Relations](https://www.nsw.gov.au/employment/rights-responsibilities/leave/long-service-leave)
- Northern Territory: [NT Government](https://nt.gov.au/employ/for-employees-in-nt/long-service-leave)
- Queensland: [Queensland Industrial Relations](https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/employing/employee-rights/long-service-leave)
- South Australia: [SafeWork SA](https://www.safework.sa.gov.au/workers/wages-and-conditions/long-service-leave)
- Tasmania: [WorkSafe Tasmania](https://worksafe.tas.gov.au/topics/laws-and-compliance/long-service-leave)
- Victoria: [Workforce Inspectorate Victoria](https://www.vic.gov.au/long-service-leave)
- Western Australia: [Department of Local Government, Industry Regulation and Safety](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/overview-of-long-service-leave-wa)

### Tip: Read our fact sheet

We have a fact sheet on long service leave that covers in detail:

- long service leave and the [National Employment StandardsThe minimum entitlements that have to be provided to all employees.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/402 "National Employment Standards (NES)")
- the interaction between state and territory laws and enterprise agreements
- minimum long service leave entitlements.

Go to the fact sheet now: [Long service leave](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/tools-and-resources/fact-sheets/minimum-workplace-entitlements/long-service-leave "Long service leave fact sheet").

## Pre-modern awards

The state and territory long service leave laws don’t apply when there are long service leave entitlements in a federal [pre-modern awardA term used by the Fair Work Ombudsman to refer to awards that existed before 1 January 2010. It includes award-based transitional instruments and transitional minimum wage instruments.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/449 "pre-modern award") that would have covered an employer and their employees before 1 January 2010.

In this case, the long service leave entitlement comes from the pre-modern award which will set out:

- how long an employee has to be working to get long service leave (for example, after 7 years)
- how much long service leave the employee gets.

### Example: Long service leave in a pre-modern award

Lesley has been working part-time for 12 years at a butcher shop.

The butcher shop is part of a chain of stores throughout Melbourne, Victoria and is covered by the Meat Award.

Under Lesley’s federal pre-modern award, there was a clause covering long service leave. This means that Lesley’s long service leave entitlement comes from her federal pre-modern award, not the Victorian long service leave legislation.

To find long service leave entitlements in a federal pre-modern award, you can:

- search for the pre-modern award using the [Find an award – Fair Work Commission](https://www.fwc.gov.au/work-conditions/awards/find-award) page
- [call us](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/contact-us/call-us "Call us") for help on federal pre-modern awards and long service leave entitlements.

Before you call us, we recommend you look at our [Before you call](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/contact-us/call-us/before-you-call "Before you call") page.

## Enterprise agreements

[Enterprise agreementsAn enterprise agreement sets out minimum employment conditions and can apply to one business or a group of businesses.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/524 "enterprise agreement") made from 1 January 2010 can include long service leave terms. This includes terms about portable long service leave and cashing out long service leave.

To find out more, go to our Library article: [Long service leave in enterprise agreements](https://library.fairwork.gov.au/viewer/?krn=K600461).

## Portable long service leave

All Australian states and territories have legislation to provide employees in some industries with access to portable long service leave. These industries include:

- [building and construction](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/leave/long-service-leave#building-and-construction)
- [contract cleaning](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/leave/long-service-leave#Contract-cleaning)
- [community services](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/leave/long-service-leave#community-services)
- [security](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/leave/long-service-leave#security).

There is also a national portable long service leave scheme for employees in the [coal mining](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/leave/long-service-leave#Coal-mining) industry.

This means an employee keeps their long service leave entitlement even if they work in different workplaces for one or more employers.

### Building and construction

For the building and construction industry, contact the authority in your state or territory:

- Australian Capital Territory: [ACT Leave](https://actleave.act.gov.au/)
- New South Wales: [Long Service Corporation](https://www.longservice.nsw.gov.au/)
- Northern Territory: [NT Build](http://www.ntbuild.com.au/)
- Queensland: [QLeave](https://www.qleave.qld.gov.au/)
- South Australia: [SA Portable Long Service Leave - Construction](https://saplsl-construction.org.au/)
- Tasmania: [TasBuild](http://www.tasbuild.com.au/)
- Victoria: [LeavePlus](https://www.leaveplus.com.au/)
- Western Australia: [MyLeave - Construction Long Service WA](http://www.myleave.wa.gov.au/)

### Coal mining

For the coal mining industry, contact [Coal Mining Industry LSL Funding Corporation](https://coallsl.com.au/).

### Contract cleaning

For the contract cleaning industry, contact the authority in your state or territory:

- Australian Capital Territory: [ACT Leave](https://actleave.act.gov.au/)
- New South Wales: [Long Service Corporation](https://www.longservice.nsw.gov.au/cci)
- Queensland: [QLeave](https://www.qleave.qld.gov.au/)
- Victoria: [Portable Long Service Authority](https://www.plsa.vic.gov.au/)

### Community services

For community services workers, contact the authority in your state or territory:

- Australian Capital Territory: [ACT Leave](https://actleave.act.gov.au/)
- New South Wales: [Long Service Corporation](https://www.longservice.nsw.gov.au/)
- Queensland: [QLeave](https://www.qleave.qld.gov.au/)
- South Australia: [SA Portable Long Service Leave](https://saplsl-community.org.au/)
- Victoria: [Portable Long Service Authority](https://www.plsa.vic.gov.au/)

### Security

For security workers, contact the authority in your state or territory:

- Australian Capital Territory: [ACT Leave](https://actleave.act.gov.au/)
- Victoria: [Portable Long Service Authority](https://www.plsa.vic.gov.au/)

## Payment for long service leave

How much an employee is paid for long service leave depends on where they get their entitlement from. Find out more from our [Payment of long service leave](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/leave/long-service-leave/payment-of-long-service-leave "Payment of long service leave") page.

Source reference for page: [Fair Work Act 2009 section 113](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text)
